04 · Case Study

Rareduft — finding the signal in 2.45M impressions.

D2C fragrance brand · Meta Ads · Jan – May 2026 · Numbers pulled directly from the Meta Ads Manager export, 13 Jun 2025 – 12 Jul 2026 reporting window.

The brief

Rareduft sells unisex Extrait de Parfum built for "working professionals" — long wear, office-safe, no reapplication. My job was to run their Meta account end-to-end: creative rotation, targeting, budget, and the organic + email layer around it.

My role

Full-funnel owner — campaign structure, ad set targeting, 38 creative variants across UGC, video, carousel and static formats, plus Instagram publishing and Mailchimp email around key promos.

01 2,449,512 Impressions
0.14% CTR
02 3,531 Link Clicks
63.4% reach LP
03 2,238 Landing Page Views
0.54% convert
04 12 Purchases (leak point)
Diagnosis 56.3% of spend → 0.37× ROAS

The "TOF Audience" ad set alone burned ₹26,041.89 — 56% of the entire account's spend — while returning just 0.37× ROAS. Flagged it and proposed a redistribution plan toward the account's proven performers.

Result 4.68× ROAS on one UGC ad

A single UGC creative ("ARP | UGC 1") returned 4.68× ROAS at ₹562 spend — proof that format and message mattered more than raw budget, and the insight that reset the brand's creative direction going forward.

Around the paid engine

In parallel, I ran the organic and email layer that kept the funnel warm: Instagram scheduling, captions and hashtags kept in step with whatever was live in Ads Manager, and Mailchimp flows for the Summer Sale and Exclusive Offer promotions — segmentation, design and open-rate / CTR tracking included.
